subject: biology
title: Farming techniques and sustainable food production
key_idea: (Separate science) A growing population needs more food, so farming and fishing must produce more without wrecking the environment. Fertilisers, pesticides, biological control and hydroponics raise yields. Fishing quotas and larger net mesh sizes keep fish stocks sustainable.

blocks.text: As the human population grows, more food is needed. This section covers why that changes how land is used and what it does to wildlife.

items.meaning: Being able to get enough food to feed a population.
The variety of living organisms in an area.
Used in a way that lets the supply last, such as fish stocks that can keep reproducing.

blocks.text: Why more land is used for farming

items: A larger population needs more crops and livestock for food.
Some crops are grown for biofuels.
Methods such as free-range and organic farming need more land for the same yield.
Peat is dug up for use as compost and as fuel.
**Deforestation** and the loss of hedgerows (to make fields larger) destroy habitats.
**Monocultures** grow a single crop, so fewer species live there.
Fertiliser run-off pollutes water.
Pesticides, insecticides and herbicides reduce insects and plants, which damages food chains.
More soil erosion follows when land is cleared.
More people need more food, so more land is farmed.
Habitat loss and chemical use reduce biodiversity.
A good answer links land use to its effect on biodiversity.

blocks.text: Farmers use several techniques to get more food from the same land. This section covers fertilisers, pesticides and hydroponics.

rows: Add minerals, such as nitrates and phosphates, to the soil
Soil that is low in minerals
Kill pests, such as insects (insecticides) and fungi (fungicides)
Crops are grown with their roots in water that contains minerals, not in soil
No soil, or soil that is unsuitable

blocks.text: Plants grow faster and better when they get the minerals they need. Less crop is lost when pests are killed. Both raise the yield.

items: Divide the plants into equal-sized groups.
Give each group a different concentration of fertiliser.
Measure the height of the plants after a period of time and find the mean increase.
The optimum is the weakest solution that gives the greatest mean growth.
Fertilisers add minerals. Pesticides kill pests. Hydroponics needs no soil.
Fertiliser run-off and pesticides can harm wildlife.
For a fair test, change the concentration and keep everything else the same.

blocks.text: **Biological control** uses another living organism, such as a predator or parasite, to reduce a pest. Examples include ladybirds eating aphids and insects used to limit prickly pear cacti.

items: The control organism is usually specific to the pest, so other species are less affected.
Biodiversity is maintained.
Chemicals do not need to be used or reapplied.
Pests do not become resistant to it in the way they can to a chemical.
Less damage to crops, so a higher yield.

blocks.text: It works best when the crop is enclosed, for example under a cover. The control organism cannot escape, so it is more likely to find and eat the pests.
Fish farming uses it too. Small fish called wrasse are kept in the cage with salmon and eat the parasites on the salmon, so more energy is available for the salmon to grow.

diagram.alt: Pick a farming problem to see which method is used to deal with it and how it helps.

options.label: Soil is low in minerals
results: Supplies the minerals the crop needs, so it grows faster and better.

options.label: There is no soil
results: Roots grow in water, so crops can be grown without soil.

options.label: Insects are eating the crop
results: Spray pesticides, or use biological control
Pesticides kill the insects. A predator such as a ladybird eats them, with no chemicals reapplied.

options.label: Parasites on farmed salmon
results: Wrasse eat the parasites, so more energy is available for the salmon to grow.

options.label: Fish stocks are falling
results: Fishing quotas and larger net mesh
Fewer fish are caught and young fish escape, so the remaining fish can reproduce.

items: Biological control uses another organism to reduce a pest.
It is specific to the pest, avoids reapplying chemicals and avoids resistance.
It works best when the crop is enclosed.

blocks.text: A growing population has caused fish stocks to decline. Fisheries are managed so that stocks recover to a sustainable level.

items: **Fishing quotas** limit the number of fish that can be caught.
**Net mesh size** is controlled so that small, young fish escape through the net.
The fish that are not caught can reproduce, so the stock recovers.

blocks.text: For example, herring only start to reproduce at 3 to 4 years old. A larger mesh lets younger fish escape and survive to reproduce.

items: Quotas limit how many fish are caught.
Large mesh lets young fish escape.
Fish that are left can reproduce, so stocks become sustainable.

checks.q: Describe how fishing quotas help return fish stocks to a sustainable level.
checks.a: Fewer fish are caught (the number of fish caught is limited), so the remaining fish can reproduce.

checks.q: Give two advantages of using biological control rather than chemical pesticides.
checks.a: Any two from: specific to the pest; maintains biodiversity; chemicals do not need to be reapplied; pests cannot become resistant; less damage to crops.

checks.q: Name the method used to grow crops with their roots in water.

exam_phrases: fewer fish caught / limit the number of fish caught

mistakes.wrong: More land is farmed, and this reduces biodiversity. (No detail on why more land is needed, or how biodiversity falls.)
mistakes.right: Answers about only land use, or only biodiversity, stay in the lower level. Describe both: why more land is needed, and how it reduces biodiversity.

mistakes.wrong: Fishing quotas mean fewer fish are caught.
mistakes.right: This earns one mark. Also say the remaining fish can reproduce, so the stock can recover.

mistakes.wrong: A larger mesh size means fewer fish are caught.
mistakes.right: Say that smaller or younger fish are not caught, so the escaping fish can reproduce.

worked_example.question:
Farming techniques have changed in recent years.

Describe:
- why more land is being used for farming
- how increased farming has decreased biodiversity.
answer_points: Why more land is used: the increasing population requires more food, from crops and livestock.
Land is also used for crops grown for biofuels, and peat is used as compost or fuel.
Free-range and organic methods use more land for the same yield.
Biodiversity: deforestation, monocultures and the loss of hedgerows cause loss of habitat.
Pesticides, insecticides and herbicides reduce insects and plants, which damages food chains.
worked_example.tip: This is a levelled answer. Facts about only land use, or only biodiversity, stay in level 1. Link the two to reach level 2.

exam_phrases: uses other organisms / different species (to reduce aphids)
chemicals do not need to be used / reapplied
less damage to the crops / increases crop yield
(biological control agent) is enclosed / cannot escape if crop is under cover
the weakest solution that allows for maximum average growth

mistakes.wrong: Aphids cannot become immune to biological control.
mistakes.right: Immune is rejected. Say the pests cannot develop resistance.

mistakes.wrong: Biological control means farmers do not need fertilisers or herbicides.
mistakes.right: Fertilisers and herbicides are ignored in this answer. Biological control replaces pesticides, so write about chemicals or insecticides.

mistakes.wrong: The optimum fertiliser concentration is the one that gives the tallest plants.
mistakes.right: The optimum is the weakest solution that allows maximum average growth. Compare the mean growth for each concentration.

worked_example.question:
Biological control can be used on aphid populations feeding on crops.

Explain the advantages of using biological control on aphid populations.
answer_points: It uses another organism, such as a ladybird, which is specific to the aphids.
It maintains biodiversity, because other species are less affected.
Chemicals do not need to be used or reapplied.
There is less damage to the crops, so the yield increases.
worked_example.tip: Link three of these points for three marks. Ladybirds, insects, predators and animals are all accepted as the control organism.

exam_phrases: more food / energy is available (for growth)
control (using) the same field and divide it into two

mistakes.wrong: If soil lacks minerals, then minerals can be added.
mistakes.right: Minerals is ignored for this answer. The word needed is fertilisers (or manure or compost).

mistakes.wrong: Hydroponics is used when soil is low in minerals.
mistakes.right: Hydroponics is for when there is no soil. Soil low in minerals is dealt with by adding fertilisers.

mistakes.wrong: The wrasse are eaten by the salmon, so the salmon grow.
mistakes.right: Salmon eating wrasse is not allowed. The wrasse eat the parasites, so more food or energy is available for the salmon to grow.

worked_example.question:
Human populations need large amounts of food to survive.

Complete these sentences about the supply of food.

Being able to get enough food to feed a population is called food ______.

Biotic factors such as ______ can prevent this happening.

Sometimes soil is not suitable to grow crops.

If soil lacks minerals, then ______ can be added.

Another option if soil is not suitable involves growing crops without soil but with the roots in water.

This is called ______.
answer_points: Biotic factors such as disease or predators (pests, pathogens and invasive species are also allowed).
If soil lacks minerals, fertilisers (manure or compost) can be added. Nitrates or phosphates are allowed.
Growing crops with the roots in water is hydroponics.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each gap. The word minerals is ignored for the third gap.
